title: A finite separable extension making all residue fields of finitely many finite extensions purely inseparable
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $K_1,\dots,K_n$ be finite field extensions of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Then there is a finite field extension $L/k$ which is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] such that for every $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$: (a) the ring $L\otimes_kK_i$ has only finitely many prime ideals; (b) for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $L\otimes_kK_i$ the quotient $(L\otimes_kK_i)/\mathfrak p$ is a field, and, regarded as an extension of $L$ through $l\mapsto l\otimes1$, it is a finite purely inseparable extension of $L$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. (One may take for $L$ a finite Galois extension of $k$ into which the separable closures $L_i$ of $k$ in $K_i$ all embed over $k$.)

source.place: Proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM (more-morphisms.tex lines 12060-12079: choice of the separable subfields L_i, of a finite Galois L receiving all L_i, and 'by our choice of L (and elementary field theory) we see that kappa(u) subset kappa(y_{i,j}) is finite purely inseparable'); field theory in Fields, Lemma 030K (fields-lemma-separable-first, line 1704), Lemma 09DT (fields-lemma-normal-closure, line 2086) and Lemma 0EXM (fields-lemma-normal-closure-galois, line 2704)

proof.text: Separable parts. Fix $i$. Since $K_i/k$ is finite, it is algebraic (each $\alpha\in K_i$ satisfies a linear dependence among $1,\alpha,\dots,\alpha^{d}$, $d=\dim_kK_i$). Let $L_i\subseteq K_i$ be the separable algebraic closure of $k$ in $K_i$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] (Stacks 030K), $L_i$ is a subfield of $K_i$ containing $k$, $L_i/k$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and $K_i/L_i$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]: if $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, every $\alpha\in K_i$ has $\alpha^{p^m}\in L_i$ for some $m\ge0$; if $\operatorname{char}k=0$, then $L_i=K_i$. Moreover $L_i/k$ is finite, $L_i$ being a $k$-subspace of the finite-dimensional $K_i$.

source.place: Proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM, lines 12062-12064 ('let kappa(s) subset L_i subset kappa(x_i) be the subfield such that L_i/kappa(s) is separable, and kappa(x_i)/L_i is purely inseparable'), by Fields, Lemma 030K (fields.tex line 1704)

proof.text: Choice of $L$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] to the finite separable algebraic extensions $L_1,\dots,L_n$ of $k$ from step 1: there are a finite field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and normal (the minimal polynomial over $k$ of every element of $L$ splits into linear factors in $L[T]$), and $k$-algebra homomorphisms $\tau_i:L_i\to L$. This $L$ is finite and separable algebraic over $k$, as the statement requires (and finite Galois, as in the parenthetical remark). It remains to check (a) and (b) for each $i$; fix $i$ and put $A=L\otimes_kK_i$, an $L$-algebra through $l\mapsto l\otimes1$.

source.place: Proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM, lines 12064-12066 ('Choose a finite Galois extension L/kappa(s) such that there exist kappa(s)-embeddings L_i -> L'); Fields, Lemmas 09DT and 0EXM

proof.text: Finitely many primes, residue fields finite over $L$. If $e_1,\dots,e_d$ is a $k$-basis of $K_i$, then every $l\otimes a$ with $a=\sum_jc_je_j$ ($c_j\in k$) equals $\sum_j(c_jl)(1\otimes e_j)$, so $1\otimes e_1,\dots,1\otimes e_d$ generate $A$ as an $L$-module: $A$ is a finite $L$-algebra. The field $L$ is a local ring whose only prime ideal is its maximal ideal $(0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] (with $R=L$, $B=A$), $A$ has only finitely many prime ideals, and each of them is maximal. This is (a). For a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, the quotient $E=A/\mathfrak p$ by the maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ is a field, and it is spanned over $L$ by the images of $1\otimes e_1,\dots,1\otimes e_d$, so $\dim_LE\le d<\infty$: $E$ is a finite field extension of $L$ through $\iota_L:L\to E$, $l\mapsto(l\otimes1)\bmod\mathfrak p$ [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM, lines 12070-12075 ('these points y_{i,j} correspond exactly to the primes in the rings kappa(u) (x)_{kappa(s)} kappa(x_i). This also explains why there are finitely many'); written out by the agent

proof.text: The image of $L_i$ lies in the image of $L$. Let $\iota_K:K_i\to E$, $a\mapsto(1\otimes a)\bmod\mathfrak p$; $\iota_L$ and $\iota_K$ are ring homomorphisms and agree on $k$ (since $c\otimes1=1\otimes c$ for $c\in k$), so both are $k$-algebra homomorphisms. Let $b\in L_i$ and let $g\in k[T]$ be its minimal polynomial over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. As $\tau_i$ is an injective $k$-algebra homomorphism, $g(\tau_i(b))=\tau_i(g(b))=0$ and $g$ is monic irreducible, so $g$ is the minimal polynomial of $\tau_i(b)\in L$; by normality of $L$ (step 2), $g=\prod_{j=1}^r(T-c_j)$ with $c_j\in L$. Applying $\iota_L$ to the coefficients (it fixes those of $g$, which lie in $k$), $g=\prod_j(T-\iota_L(c_j))$ in $E[T]$. Since $g(\iota_K(b))=\iota_K(g(b))=0$ and $E$ is a field, $\iota_K(b)=\iota_L(c_j)$ for some $j$. Hence $\iota_K(L_i)\subseteq\iota_L(L)$.

source.place: Proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM, lines 12076-12079 ('By our choice of L (and elementary field theory) we see that kappa(u) subset kappa(y_{i,j}) is finite purely inseparable'); the elementary field theory written out by the agent

proof.text: $E/L$ is purely inseparable. Every element of $A$ is a finite sum $\sum_rl_r\otimes a_r=\sum_r(l_r\otimes1)(1\otimes a_r)$, so every element of $E$ has the form $x=\sum_r\iota_L(l_r)\iota_K(a_r)$ ($l_r\in L$, $a_r\in K_i$). If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, then $K_i=L_i$ (step 1), so $\iota_K(a_r)\in\iota_L(L)$ by step 4 and $x\in\iota_L(L)$: $\iota_L$ is onto, $E=L$, which is the meaning of purely inseparable in characteristic $0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, then $E$ has characteristic $p$ (it is a $k$-algebra); choose by step 1 integers $m_r$ with $a_r^{p^{m_r}}\in L_i$ and put $m=\max_rm_r$, so $a_r^{p^m}=(a_r^{p^{m_r}})^{p^{m-m_r}}\in L_i$ for all $r$. Since $y\mapsto y^{p^m}$ is a ring endomorphism of $E$, $x^{p^m}=\sum_r\iota_L(l_r^{p^m})\,\iota_K(a_r^{p^m})$, which lies in $\iota_L(L)$ by step 4. So every element of $E$ has a $p$-power in $L$, and with step 3, $E$ is a finite purely inseparable extension of $L$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. This is (b).

lean.statement: theorem exists_separable_split_purelyInseparable_prime_quotients (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (K : Fin n → Type v) [∀ i : Fin n, Field (K i)] [∀ i : Fin n, Algebra k (K i)] [∀ i : Fin n, Module.Finite k (K i)] : ∃ (L : Type (max u v)) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L), Module.Finite k L ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable k L ∧ IsGalois k L ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, Nonempty (separableClosure k (K i) →ₐ[k] L)) ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, Finite (PrimeSpectrum (L ⊗[k] K i)) ∧ ∀ (p : Ideal (L ⊗[k] K i)), p.IsPrime → IsField ((L ⊗[k] K i) ⧸ p) ∧ Module.Finite L ((L ⊗[k] K i) ⧸ p) ∧ IsPurelyInseparable L ((L ⊗[k] K i) ⧸ p)
lean.note: The Galois witness and embeddings of the relative separable closures render the parenthetical clause as well as the main conclusion. IsField uses the canonical quotient ring operations; the canonical quotient L-algebra is induced from the left-factor tensor-product algebra.
